body:
N-26 DESIGN, part 2: decisions I made (yours to overrule) and what I most want the advisor to decide.

DECIDED: (1) Trust set as in the detail note; an unknown or missing videoType on an available entry with no album is an upload (the safe default never promotes an uploader to a performer). (2) Slice 1 is the two root causes ONLY: my first, wider context-word list (op, ed, ost, session, any "live in") broke good titles: "Ed Sheeran - Stand By Me" gave artist "Me", "Chopin - Nocturne Op. 9 No. 2 | Piano" the uploader, "We Live in Fear" artist "We". The tightened shapes (series label ending in Opening/Ending, "by" only after it, "live at" only after a comma or colon) fix all three audit strings and change none of 17 titles that are right today; they are slice 4 with a negative corpus (prototype in scratch, not committed). (3) Store the FACTS (artist_basis, uploader) on the ref, not just a verdict, so a later, better rule re-derives offline. (4) Slice 5 (repair of stored rows) is NOT built now: the test server's rows are test data (reset and re-import), no stranger has a library yet (no public image, join/invite not walked, P2-11 closed for the same reason). That is true ONLY if slices 1+2 are in the FIRST public image: add it to RELEASE-CANDIDATE.md as a gate; trigger for slice 5 = any install other than the owner's test server holding an older import. (5) The file import is left alone: a real takeout file is needed to know whether an upload row carries the channel. (6) MATCHER_REVISION stays 1.

FOR THE ADVISOR: (a) OMV is trusted from ONE recording (Lil Wayne, in playlist_community.json): step 0 must record an OMV uploaded by a LABEL channel before slice 1 merges; if YouTube Music shows the label there, OMV leaves the trusted set. (b) Is deferring slice 5 right, or build the repair now? Repair sketch: a row is recognised exactly when its stored artist equals the uploader and the new reading differs; kept files under Encore/KEXP/ need tags rewritten, a new folder and a scan (the keeper has no such step; a moved file is a new song id for the music server); a changed norm_key may collide with another ref (index not unique: the B-71 situation, no merge by name). (c) Slice 3: if the tag proof fails, the way out is album = the channel (a collection per uploader) rather than an Unknown Artist bucket (rejected as the general answer: it loses a performer's own channel and a reciter's). (d) Is slice 4 worth its false positives at all, given U1 and U2 stay unknowable?

Not done / not changed by this design: B-118/B-119 joined credits ("A & B" stay one artist string, as today), the Unicode normaliser of P2-25 (the new whole-name test is Unicode-safe on its own and should move onto the P2-25 function when it exists), the 50+ channel artists already on VM 108.
